views.name: dicom_instance_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "SOPInstanceUID" AS sop_instance_uid,
  "StudyInstanceUID" AS study_instance_uid,
  "SeriesInstanceUID" AS series_instance_uid,
  "SOPClassUID" AS sop_class_uid,
  "Modality" AS modality,
  "PatientID" AS patient_id,
  "PatientName" AS patient_name,
  "PatientBirthDate"::DATE AS patient_birth_date,
  "PatientSex" AS patient_sex,
  "StudyDate"::DATE AS study_date,
  "SeriesDate"::DATE AS series_date,
  "AcquisitionDate"::DATE AS acquisition_date,
  "InstanceCreationDate"::DATE AS instance_creation_date,
  "StudyTime" AS study_time,
  "SeriesTime" AS series_time,
  "InstanceCreationTime" AS instance_creation_time,
  "SeriesDescription" AS series_description,
  "StudyDescription" AS study_description,
  "Manufacturer" AS manufacturer,
  "InstitutionName" AS institution_name,
  "LengthToEnd"::NUMBER AS length_to_end,
  "ReferencedSOPInstanceUIDInFile" AS referenced_sop_in_file,
  "ReferencedFileID" AS referenced_file_id,
  "ImageType" AS image_type,
  "PixelBandwidth" AS pixel_bandwidth
FROM IDC.IDC_V17.DICOM_METADATA
grain: sop_instance_uid, one row per DICOM instance (file)
views.description: Normalized projection of core DICOM instance-level attributes from IDC.IDC_V17.DICOM_METADATA. Use this as the canonical per-instance row for joins, filtering and aggregations. Casts and aliases provide stable column names and expose common identifiers and key descriptive/temporal attributes. | Use for: List instances for a patient/study/series; Filter images by modality, manufacturer or date range; Join instance metadata to segmentation or measurement tables; Compute counts of instances per series/study/patient

views.name: dicom_series_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "SeriesInstanceUID" AS series_instance_uid,
  "StudyInstanceUID" AS study_instance_uid,
  MIN("StudyDate"::DATE) AS min_study_date,
  MAX("StudyDate"::DATE) AS max_study_date,
  MIN("SeriesDate"::DATE) AS min_series_date,
  MAX("SeriesDate"::DATE) AS max_series_date,
  COUNT(1) AS instance_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT "SOPInstanceUID") AS distinct_instance_count,
  MIN("InstanceCreationDate"::DATE) AS first_instance_creation_date,
  MAX("InstanceCreationDate"::DATE) AS last_instance_creation_date
FROM IDC.IDC_V17.DICOM_METADATA
GROUP BY "SeriesInstanceUID", "StudyInstanceUID"
grain: series_instance_uid, one row per DICOM series
views.description: Per-series aggregated measures derived from DICOM_METADATA: counts and basic date range metrics. Use this to summarize series-level volume and temporal span. Keeps series and study identifiers for joins. | Use for: How many instances are in each series?; Series-level temporal coverage and freshness; Join series-level summaries to segmentation or curated series tables

views.name: dicom_latest_instance_per_series
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "SeriesInstanceUID" AS series_instance_uid,
  "SOPInstanceUID" AS sop_instance_uid,
  "InstanceCreationDate"::DATE AS instance_creation_date,
  "InstanceCreationTime" AS instance_creation_time,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "SeriesInstanceUID" ORDER BY "InstanceCreationDate"::DATE DESC, "InstanceCreationTime" DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn
FROM IDC.IDC_V17.DICOM_METADATA
grain: series_instance_uid, one row per instance with a rank; use rn = 1 to pick latest
views.description: Latest instance per series using instance_creation_date/time. Exposes a rank so downstream queries can select top-N per series. Useful for selecting a representative or most recent instance per series. | Use for: Select the most recent instance for each series; De-duplicate series by taking latest instance; Create a downsampled representative image per series for QC

views.name: dicom_patient_study_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "PatientID" AS patient_id,
  COUNT(1) AS instance_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT "StudyInstanceUID") AS distinct_study_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT "SeriesInstanceUID") AS distinct_series_count,
  MIN("StudyDate"::DATE) AS first_study_date,
  MAX("StudyDate"::DATE) AS last_study_date
FROM IDC.IDC_V17.DICOM_METADATA
GROUP BY "PatientID"
views.description: Per-patient summary counts and study diversity. Aggregates instances and distinct studies for each patient_id. Useful for patient-level cohorts and join keys for clinical data. | Use for: Cohort size by patient; Patients with multiple studies or series; Patient-level temporal coverage

views.name: dicom_image_type_exploded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm."SOPInstanceUID" AS sop_instance_uid,
  dm."SeriesInstanceUID" AS series_instance_uid,
  dm."StudyInstanceUID" AS study_instance_uid,
  f.value::STRING AS image_type_element
FROM IDC.IDC_V17.DICOM_METADATA dm,
LATERAL FLATTEN(input=>dm."ImageType") f
grain: sop_instance_uid + image_type_element, one row per image type element per instance
views.description: Unnest/flatten the VARIANT ImageType field into one row per image_type element for each instance. Useful when ImageType is stored as an array and downstream filters must match elements (e.g., ORIGINAL/PRIMARY). | Use for: Filter instances by ImageType elements (e.g., ORIGINAL, DERIVED); Count how many instances have specific image type flags; Join image-type-specific instances to segmentation/analysis results
